title: St. Paul's Cathedral, Mdina
visualBrief: Individual St. Paul’s Cathedral, Mdina: warm Maltese limestone Baroque west front with paired clock/bell towers and curved stone spires, central triangular pediment/cross, paired pilasters, three recessed wooden portals and large upper arched window. Broad lower flat-roof aisles, eastward central nave/crossing, large octagonal windowed drum, low weathered metal dome with stone ribs/scrolls and small lantern/cross. Sparse side windows, cornices, stone diamonds/crest and short front steps. Five existing shared ashlar/limestone/granite/standing-seam-metal/wood graphs, linear tints, metric UVs, flat architectural normals and four browser levels. Exact carving/heraldry/clock numerals, full interiors/bells, hidden rear windows/roof joins and surveyed plaza/thresholds remain approximate or excluded.

Skyline keeps paired curved stone tower spires, central pediment, octagonal drum/dome/lantern and low nave/aisle forms. District adds shared surfaces, clock faces, flat glazing/belfry bays and selected trim. Street adds actual recesses/open belfries, capitals/pilasters, larger mullions and dome ribs. Closeup/master refine surrounds, window bars, spire ribs and clock marks. Small lantern windows remain flat fields. Synthetic cottages are a review fixture.
